page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance features 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, and lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is capped at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance's performance in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests rank in the bottom 25%, with scores of 1102.39 and 2936.9 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate weak to poor performance, with uncached large-block read speeds falling into the bottom 10% at 21.08 GB/sec. Similarly, text and image processing benchmarks under Geekbench, alongside Redis SET operations, register in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.g5.xlarge offers a stable resource profile for entry-level workloads. However, its low benchmark scores relative to modern hardware suggest a performance-per-resource tradeoff, making it less suitable for compute-intensive or high-throughput database tasks. It is best utilized for lightweight web serving, basic application hosting, or small-scale development and testing environments that do not require high-speed local storage or rapid memory access.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor with a KVM hypervisor. It operates on an x86_64 architecture with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Network performance is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Across multiple benchmarks, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark, the instance consistently performs in the bottom 10% to 25%, indicating weak processing and memory bandwidth capabilities. Given these performance tradeoffs, the ecs.g5.xlarge is best suited for low-demand workloads such as lightweight static web serving, basic application hosting, and development environments where resource stability is required but high-throughput processing is not critical.
